passage: At the art table in Class One, Keerthana leaned over to look at the picture beside hers. Sahil had drawn a sun with long, wavy rays and a tiny bird on a wire. "Your drawing is so good!" she said, and felt a smile spread on her own face. She looked at her own sun, which was just a yellow circle. "Will you show me how you did the rays?" Sahil grinned and handed her a crayon. "Start with a line, then wiggle."

qa.q: What did Sahil draw on a wire?
qa.a: He drew a tiny bird on a wire.

qa.q: How did Keerthana feel when she told Sahil his drawing was good?
qa.a: She felt happy to give kind words. Her spreading smile and her wish to learn from him show admiration without envy.

qa.q: Why was asking "Will you show me?" a wise next step?
qa.a: It turned admiration into learning, and Sahil could share what he knows. She gets better at drawing rays and they both enjoy it. 😊

qa.q: How might Sahil feel when Keerthana praises his picture and asks for help?
qa.a: He probably feels proud and glad to be asked. He grinned and gave her a crayon, so he seems happy to share the trick.

grounding: I tell my friend her drawing is so good, feel happy and ask her to show me how.

passage: In the supermarket queue Omar spotted the sweets and Ivan said, "Not today." Omar's face crumpled. He screamed and threw himself down on the tiles, arms and legs flailing, as though his body were too big for him. People glanced over. Ivan did not shout. He crouched beside Omar and said, "No sweets today. I am here. Let's smell a flower and blow out a candle." He breathed slowly, and after a while Omar copied him.

qa.q: Where did Omar throw himself down?
qa.a: He threw himself down on the tiles in the supermarket queue.

qa.q: What was Omar feeling when he screamed and flailed on the floor?
qa.a: He was overwhelmed with anger about the sweets, and his body felt too big to control.

qa.q: What did Ivan do that helped, and what did he keep?
qa.a: He stayed calm, crouched beside Omar and helped him breathe, and he still kept the limit: no sweets today.

qa.q: How might Ivan feel while people glance at Omar's screaming in the queue?
qa.a: He may feel a bit self-conscious, but he stays focused on Omar. His slow breathing shows he is choosing to stay calm.

grounding: The child screams and throws himself down over no sweets; a calm grown-up keeps the limit and helps him breathe.

passage: The bus to the fair was due in minutes and Jomon was rushing Seema along the pavement when she spotted a stall of glittery bangles. "I want them!" she cried. Jomon slowed and crouched. "I know you are upset. The answer is still no." Seema's lip wobbled and tears came. He did not change his mind or raise his voice. He held her hand while she cried, and when the bus rounded the corner she wiped her nose and climbed on beside him.

qa.q: What did Seema want from the stall?
qa.a: She wanted the glittery bangles.

qa.q: Why did Seema feel safe even though she was crying?
qa.a: Jomon stayed calm and did not give in, so she could feel that the limit was steady and he was still with her.

qa.q: What did Jomon do well under time pressure?
qa.a: He slowed down, said he knew she was upset and kept the answer as no, holding her hand while she cried. 🙂

qa.q: What might Jomon have been worried about while the bus was due?
qa.a: He may have been worried about missing the bus, but did not let the hurry make him snap. He put Seema's feelings first for a moment.

grounding: My parent calmly says I know you are upset, the answer is still no; the limit does not break and the big feeling passes.

passage: Oskar wanted to keep watching the video and Sofia said it was time to stop. He howled and kicked the sofa. "Stop it now or you will never watch anything again!" Sofia shouted. Oskar went silent. His breath hitched and he stared at her, frightened. Later, in the quiet, Sofia knelt beside him. "I shouted and that scared you. I am sorry. Big feelings are not your fault." She hugged him, and after a moment he leaned in.

qa.q: What did Oskar kick?
qa.a: He kicked the sofa.

qa.q: Why did Oskar go silent after Sofia shouted?
qa.a: He was frightened, so he stopped crying, but that does not mean he learned anything. His hitching breath and stare show fear.

qa.q: What did Sofia do that repaired the moment?
qa.a: Afterwards she knelt, apologised for shouting, said big feelings are not his fault and hugged him. That calmer repair helps more than the threat.

qa.q: How might Sofia feel when she remembers the shouting later?
qa.a: She may feel regret and worry that she scared him. Her apology shows she cares, and wants to handle the next tantrum more calmly.

grounding: A parent shouts and threatens during the tantrum; the child is frightened, and a calm repair with a hug and explanation helps.

passage: At the school winter bazaar, Swati had screamed and thrown her cap when Yogesh would not buy the toy at the stall. Now she stood by the notice board with her face hidden in his coat. Her cheeks burned and her voice was tiny. "Sorry, Papa." Yogesh stroked her back. "You were upset. It is over. Let's fix it." He did not say she was bad. Together they picked up the cap and walked to the stall to say sorry.

qa.q: Where was Swati hiding her face?
qa.a: She stood by the notice board with her face hidden in his coat.

qa.q: What was Swati feeling when she said "Sorry, Papa" in a tiny voice?
qa.a: She felt embarrassed and sorry about the tantrum. Hiding her face and burning cheeks show her shame.

qa.q: How did Yogesh help Swati without making the shame stick?
qa.a: He said she was upset, that it was over and that they could fix it, and he did not call her bad. Then they went to say sorry together.

qa.q: How might the person at the stall see Swati coming back to say sorry?
qa.a: They probably see a child who is trying to put things right. It may leave them feeling kindly toward her, and it helps the moment end.

grounding: After the tantrum I feel embarrassed and sorry and hide my face; a parent says you were upset, it is over, let us fix it.

passage: Heavy rain cancelled the trip to the park. Salma's bucket and spade sat by the door. "It's not fair!" She stamped and felt her face get hot. Then she grabbed her teddy, hugged it hard and blew out slowly, as if at a birthday candle, three times. "I am angry," she said in a small voice. Elizabeth, her mother, nodded. "I hear you." Salma's shoulders dropped. "I did it myself, Mummy." She looked proud.

qa.q: What was left by the door?
qa.a: Salma's bucket and spade sat by the door.

qa.q: What did Salma feel after she calmed herself?
qa.a: She felt proud that she had managed her anger herself, as her words "I did it myself, Mummy" show. 😊

qa.q: Which small steps did Salma use, and why do they matter?
qa.a: She hugged her teddy, blew birthday-candle breaths and said "I am angry." Naming the feeling and doing a small calming action are the first steps of self-control.

qa.q: How might Elizabeth see Salma's calming down on a rainy day?
qa.a: She probably feels glad and a little surprised that her daughter handled disappointment so well. Saying "I hear you" let Salma do it herself.

grounding: I hug my teddy, blow candle breaths and say I am angry; I feel proud when I calm down.

passage: In the classroom, Bhupen lost his turn on the toy drum and burst into a huge tantrum. He screamed, stamped and kicked a chair. Sabina froze by the shelf with her heart thumping and felt scared and unsure what to do. She took a step back, then walked quickly to the teacher's desk. "Bhupen is very upset," she said. The teacher went over. Later, when Bhupen was calmer, Sabina sat beside him. "Do you want to colour with me?"

qa.q: What did Bhupen kick?
qa.a: He kicked a chair.

qa.q: What was Sabina feeling when she froze by the shelf?
qa.a: She was scared and unsure. Her thumping heart shows she did not know how to help.

qa.q: What did Sabina do that was wise, and what did she not have to do?
qa.a: She stepped back, told the teacher and was kind to him later. She did not have to fix his feelings herself, because big feelings are not dangerous.

qa.q: How might Bhupen feel when Sabina offers to colour with him later?
qa.a: He may feel relieved and a little embarrassed, but glad someone still wants to be with him. Her invitation says she is still his friend.

grounding: A friend has a huge tantrum and I feel scared; I step back, tell a teacher and am kind later.

passage: I am Avni, Jomon's big sister. In the toy shop our mother said no to the robot he wanted. Jomon's face went red and he stamped his foot. He crossed his arms and would not look at her. I could not tell what he felt exactly, but his chin shook like he was about to cry. Then he took a breath and said, "Can I have it on my birthday?" Mother smiled. "We can think about it then." He nodded and held her hand.

qa.q: What did Jomon ask his mother for at the end?
qa.a: He asked, "Can I have it on my birthday?"

qa.q: What might Jomon have been feeling when he crossed his arms and would not look at his mother?
qa.a: He seems furious and maybe hurt, as if his mother did not love him right now. Avni admits she cannot be sure.

qa.q: Why was asking "Can I have it on my birthday?" a wise move?
qa.a: It replaced screaming with a request, and it gave his mother something to say yes to. It also kept things calm between them.

qa.q: How might the shop scene look from Jomon's mother's side?
qa.a: She probably felt she had to hold the no, and was relieved and pleased when he chose to ask instead of scream.

grounding: My parent said no to the toy and I am furious; a wise child asks if he can have it on his birthday.

passage: The cartoon ended and Kamal turned to the kitchen. "Mummy, one more show?" Rukmini looked up from the dal. "No, beta. It's bedtime soon, and tomorrow you can watch another." Kamal's lip stuck out and he grumbled, "Always no." But he stood up and dragged his feet to the bathroom anyway. She always tells me why, he thought. When Rukmini came to tuck him in, he held her hand and yawned. 🙂

qa.q: What did Kamal ask Rukmini for?
qa.a: He asked, "Mummy, one more show?"

qa.q: Why did Kamal go to the bathroom even though he grumbled?
qa.a: He trusts that his mother has a good reason, since she always tells him why. His grumbling was small.

qa.q: What makes Rukmini's no work well for a child like Kamal?
qa.a: It is kind and consistent, with a reason and a promise for tomorrow. Over time that helps Kamal accept rules without a fight. 😊

qa.q: How might Rukmini feel when Kamal grumbles but goes anyway?
qa.a: She is probably a little amused and relieved that he accepts it. She may also feel encouraged that her steady rule is working.

grounding: I ask for one more show and hear no; I grumble but trust my parent has a good reason.

passage: At the temple fair Kashish begged for a second jalebi, and Sachin shook his head. "No, beta. You had one." Her face crumpled. "You are mean! I hate you!" The words flew out, and then her stomach turned over as she saw his face. She pressed herself against his leg and hid her eyes. Sachin crouched down and said gently, "You are angry, and I still love you." Kashish sniffed and looked up, a little frightened, and he wiped her cheek.

qa.q: What did Kashish ask for at the temple fair?
qa.a: She begged for a second jalebi.

qa.q: Why did Kashish hide her eyes after she said "I hate you"?
qa.a: She was angry, but she was also afraid of what she had said and that it might change her father's love.

qa.q: What did Sachin say that helped Kashish, and why?
qa.a: He said, "You are angry, and I still love you." That teaches her hard words do not end love, so she can settle.

qa.q: How might Sachin feel when Kashish shouts that he is mean?
qa.a: It probably stings, but he sees a small child who is upset. He stays gentle so that she knows he is not going away.

grounding: I say you are mean, I hate you and feel angry and afraid; a parent replies you are angry, I still love you.
